note: Declarative input to capture_growth.mjs. Each claim names the page it is read from and the state it is published in. A claim moves to CLAIM_MEASURED only where a measurement id resolves to a CLAIM_MEASURED harness output; where the harness returns UNMEASURED the claim stays UNMEASURED and the reason is carried. Nothing here is written by hand into a measured state.
selection_rule: Organisations and projects adjacent to what we measure: AI assurance and governance platforms, AI evaluation and observability platforms, AI underwriters, frontier model providers, open-source agent-harness and guardrail frameworks, two public tokenised-settlement programmes, and the maintainer itself (spec 10.6). Within each, the claims selected are those specific enough to capture verbatim and about infrastructure a third party relies on. For the open-source projects the claims are read from each project's OWN repository file, never from press coverage and never from a list handed to us; where a project states a limit on what it does, that statement is captured on the same footing as any other, because a scoped claim is a result and not an absence. No organisation is entered here, or implied to be entered here, on the basis of belonging to any body, alliance or programme: membership is not a claim, it is not captured, and it is not inferred.

One reading is not a series; this stays unmeasured until at least two dated points exist.

subjects.name: Anthropic
conflicts: The maintainer's capture tooling for this run was operated through a language model supplied by this subject. No payment, sponsorship or agreement of any kind runs between the maintainer and this subject, and nothing about what is captured, measured or published here was requested by, shown to, or influenced by it. Disclosed at artifact level because a reader of this one record should see it (spec 10.3).

claims.verbatim: Anthropic is a public benefit corporation dedicated to securing its benefits and mitigating its risks.
claims.plan: the corporate form is recorded in a US state's public company register, which is the one element a stranger can check. Query that register for the entity and record what it returns. Not run in this pass: the register this maintainer reached answers an automated reader with a challenge, and a search that was turned away must never be published as an absence.

claims.verbatim: Our most capable Opus model, faster and costs 40% less to run.
claims.plan: the cost element is settleable against the subject's own published price list, which is the claim again rather than evidence about it (spec 4.6); the capability and speed elements rest on evaluations this maintainer cannot re-run without payment. Capture weekly with the page digest and record every revision.

claims.verbatim: Mistral raises €3B to make sovereign, open-weight AI the technology frontier

No participant is named in this headline; read the subject's own linked announcement for the names and corroborate against each one's own record.

claims.verbatim: In-region inference, open models, and new European infrastructure for sovereign AI

claims.plan: a dated commitment with a stated horizon. It becomes settleable from the publisher's own service documentation and the participating infrastructures' own records on its resolution date; until then no measurement is run and none is implied.

claims.plan: a dated deliverable. On its resolution date, settleable by whether a blueprint document is published by the named parties; until then no measurement is run.

claims.uncheckable_reason: A characterisation of legal effect. No public dataset settles it; only a court or the regulator itself could, and neither has been asked. A statement about the evidence available to the public, never about the subject.

claims.verbatim: Stage II: Enablement of secondary-market trading, with access extended to retail participants.
claims.plan: a staged commitment published without a date, so no resolution date can be recorded for it and none is invented. Watch the publisher's own circulars and press releases for the enabling instrument and measure against it when one appears.

subjects.name: Council of AI (CSOAI Ltd)
conflicts: This subject IS the maintainer. Every claim here is the maintainer's own, captured and published under the same rules as every other subject, because a body that observes others' claims and exempts its own is running a campaign rather than applying a discipline (spec 10.6). The conflict is total and is stated rather than managed.

claims.verbatim: We measure how AI systems behave, and sign the answer so you never take our word for it
claims.plan: settleable by a stranger: fetch any published signed record keylessly, recompute its digest and check its Ed25519 signature against the DID document at the maintainer's apex. A signature either verifies or it does not, and that answer does not depend on the maintainer's assertion. Run it over a sample with a published selection rule and report the pass count with its denominator.

claims.verbatim: Verification is free forever — no login, no fee, no tier benefit
claims.plan: the part of this claim that public evidence can reach today is whether a stranger with no account is served by the verification surfaces: request each published verification door with no credential and record the HTTP status. The word 'forever' is about future action and no measurement can reach it; that part stays unmeasured permanently and the artifact says so.

claims.verbatim: Every answer graded by a rule, never by another AI
claims.plan: settleable from the published grader source and the published graded rows: read the grader, then check that every published row carries a rule identifier and a quoted match rather than a model score. Report the count with its denominator. Not run in this pass.

claims.verbatim: 23 axis · 23 measured on the board today
claims.plan: restatement watch, and held to exactly the standard applied to every other subject: the only enumeration of this figure is the maintainer's own board API, so recomputing it from that API would be the claim again rather than evidence about it (spec 4.6). Capture weekly with the page digest and record every revision, including any downward one.

claims.verbatim: The NeMo Guardrails library enables developers building LLM-based applications to add **programmable guardrails** between the application code and the LLM.
claims.uncheckable_reason: A description of where the library sits in an application. It names no quantity, no rate and no threshold, so there is nothing a third party can recompute from public evidence. A statement about the evidence available to the public, never about the project.

claims.verbatim: No user content is collected in the event payload.
claims.plan: this is a guarantee about behaviour, and the behaviour is in the same public repository as the claim. It is settleable by reading the telemetry code path and the event schema it builds, and by running the library offline and reading the audit file it writes. Neither was done in this pass, and the claim is not treated as checked because the source is open.

claims.verbatim: Audit writes are best effort, and telemetry transmission still proceeds if local audit writing fails.
claims.plan: a limitation the project states about its own behaviour, which is the kind of claim that costs a publisher something to make. It is settleable from the same public repository by reading the audit write path and its error handling. Not run in this pass.

claims.verbatim: NVIDIA Build is intended for evaluation and testing only and must not be used in production environments.
claims.uncheckable_reason: A restriction the publisher places on a third party's service. It is an instruction to the reader, not a quantity, and no public evidence settles whether an instruction is followed. A statement about the evidence, never about the project.

claims.verbatim: `garak` probes for hallucination, data leakage, prompt injection, misinformation, toxicity generation, jailbreaks, and many other weaknesses.
claims.plan: an enumeration of what the tool probes for, and the probes are in the same public repository. It is settleable by listing the probe modules the published package actually ships and mapping each named category onto them, reporting the categories with no shipped probe as unmapped rather than as absent. Not run in this pass.

claims.verbatim: `garak` checks if an LLM can be made to fail in a way we don't want.
claims.uncheckable_reason: The success condition is 'a way we don't want', which the sentence leaves to the reader. No public evidence settles a claim whose criterion is undefined in the claim. A statement about the evidence, never about the project.

claims.verbatim: `garak`'s a free tool.
claims.plan: read the licence the code host's own detector reports for the named repository, and the text of the licence file itself. Neither is written by the claimant, which is what makes it evidence about the claim rather than the claim again.

claims.verbatim: Guardrails is a Python framework that helps build reliable AI applications by performing two key functions:
claims.uncheckable_reason: 'Reliable' is not defined in the claim and no public dataset settles whether an application built with a framework is reliable. A statement about the evidence available to the public, never about the project.

claims.verbatim: Yes, Guardrails can be used with proprietary and open-source LLMs.
claims.plan: settleable from the published package: enumerate the model integrations it ships and check that the set spans both proprietary and open-weight providers. The denominator is the integrations shipped, not the models that exist. Not run in this pass.

claims.verbatim:
The Python Risk Identification Tool for generative AI (PyRIT) is an open source
framework built to empower security professionals and engineers to proactively
identify risks in generative AI systems.
claims.plan: only one element of this compound sentence is settleable by public evidence: whether the named repository is open source, which the code host's own record answers without the claimant's help. The rest of the sentence describes an intended effect on a user and stays unmeasured.
claims.measures_only: the open-source element of this sentence, and nothing else in it. 'Empower' and 'proactively identify risks' name an intended effect on a user, and no public evidence measures an effect on a user; those elements are unmeasured

claims.verbatim: Components within the Purple Llama project will be licensed permissively enabling both research and commercial usage.
claims.plan: read the licence the code host's own detector reports for the named repository, and the text of the licence file itself. Neither is written by the claimant, which is what makes it evidence about the claim rather than the claim again.

claims.verbatim: CyberSec Eval v1 was what we believe was the first industry-wide set of cybersecurity safety evaluations for LLMs.
claims.plan: a priority claim, and the publisher has hedged it in its own words ('what we believe was'). The honest outside test of a priority claim is a documented earlier example from some other party's own published materials, dated. Searching the public record for an earlier industry-wide LLM cybersecurity evaluation suite is settleable in principle and was not run in this pass; until it is, nothing is concluded, and the hedge is recorded as the publisher wrote it.

claims.verbatim: Llama Guard 3 consists of a series of high-performance input and output moderation models designed to support developers to detect various common types of violating content.
claims.plan: 'high-performance' over 'various common types' is settleable only against a named benchmark and a named taxonomy. The same repository names the taxonomy it targets, and public evaluation sets for it exist, so a measurement is possible in principle; it needs model inference this pass did not run. No number is invented in its place.

claims.verbatim: Invariant Guardrails is a comprehensive rule-based guardrailing layer for LLM or MCP-powered AI applications.
claims.plan: 'comprehensive' is a coverage claim over a category the sentence does not bound. The answerable version is a counterexample log: whether other projects' own documentation describes rule-based guardrailing over the same surfaces, quoted from their own materials. Not run in this pass.

claims.verbatim: It is deployed between your application and your MCP servers or LLM provider, allowing for continuous steering and monitoring, without invasive code changes.
claims.plan: 'without invasive code changes' is settleable from the published integration path: whether the documented deployment requires an application code change at all, or only a configuration or proxy endpoint change. Readable from the same public repository. Not run in this pass.

claims.verbatim: Guardrails is an open source project by [Invariant Labs](https://invariantlabs.ai).
claims.plan: read the licence the code host's own detector reports for the named repository, and the text of the licence file itself. Neither is written by the claimant, which is what makes it evidence about the claim rather than the claim again.

claims.plan: read the licence the code host's own detector reports for the named repository, and the text of the licence file itself. Neither is written by the claimant, which is what makes it evidence about the claim rather than the claim again.

claims.verbatim: These are not planned for v3.
claims.plan: a statement about what the project will NOT carry forward, which is the kind of claim a publisher gains nothing by making. claims.verbatim: Built-in evals include string matching, comparisons, regex, semantic similarity, and LLM-as-judge checks (`Groundedness`, `Conformity`, `LLMJudge`).
claims.plan: an enumeration settleable against the published package: import it and list the evaluators it actually exposes, reporting any named here with no shipped implementation as unmapped rather than as absent. Not run in this pass.
